title: Adobe and Microsoft bring AI editing and Express templates to Windows Photos
summary: Adobe and Microsoft integrate AI editing features and Express templates into Windows Photos
detailed: Adobe and Microsoft are expanding access to Adobe’s creative tools on Windows PCs, with updates for professional creative applications and the integration of Adobe Express features into Microsoft Photos.

sentences: Adobe and Microsoft are expanding access to Adobe’s creative tools on Windows PCs, with updates for professional creative applications and the integration of Adobe Express features into Microsoft Photos.
Announced at Adobe MAX, the collaboration includes optimised versions of Photoshop, Premiere, After Effects and Substance 3D Painter (beta) for high-performance Arm-based Windows PCs.
The applications are designed to support AI processing, editing, colour correction and visual effects.
The optimised applications will be available on devices including the new Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark.
The updates are intended to improve performance for demanding creative and technical workflows.
Photoshop has been rearchitected to improve responsiveness on Arm-based Windows PCs.
Its Remove tool uses on-device generative AI to remove unwanted elements and generate replacement content.
Adobe is also developing a compositing-based architecture for the application, which will support live filters, HDR and brushing capabilities.
Premiere has an optimised video pipeline for playback, colour correction and rendering.
The updates also improve the performance of features such as Enhance Speech and Object Mask.
Users can move projects to After Effects for further editing, with the application receiving similar optimisations.
Substance 3D Painter (beta) has also been optimised for Arm-based Windows PCs.
The update is intended to improve performance when working with large 3D assets, texture sets and GPU-intensive tasks such as baking mesh maps.

Speaking on the development, James Howell, Vice President, Windows Consumer Marketing, Microsoft, said, “Microsoft’s partnership with Adobe is about giving creators more ways to create on Windows, from the apps and capabilities needed for demanding professional work to quick and easy tools for everyday projects.

Whatever they’re making, we want creators to have the choice and tools to do it on the Windows PC that’s right for them.”
The companies are also bringing Adobe-powered editing features and Adobe Express templates to Microsoft Photos on Windows 11.
A preview is expected to be available to Windows Insiders in the coming months.
The features will allow users to extend the edges of photos, rotate images without cropping and use AI tools to add, change or remove objects.
The application will also let users open photos in Adobe Express from Photo Viewer and use templates to create invitations, flyers and social media posts.
The collaboration will include further benchmarking and optimisation of Adobe’s applications for Windows devices.
